claim: Lock-resolution follow-up on the same pre-layout ro_array_core (issue #288, DR-0012 follow-up 5): 200-edge observation windows resolving +-0.1 % detuning (0.1-cycle drift criterion, 2x margin; a free-running ring detuned by delta slips delta*(N-1) cycles over N edges) with a 400-edge convergence subset; detuning ladder +-0.1 / +-0.25 / +-0.4 % on both sides of each ring's own frequency at 20 and 50 mV pk (inside the #200 10-50 mV lock bracket) and +-0.25 % at 5 mV pk (below its 10 mV floor); on-frequency rows kept drift-UNRESOLVED and decided, where at all, by detuned neighbours and pull evidence; current-injection controls at own/+2/+5/+20 % detuning against the clean free-running reference; LOCK, Q and BIAS reported separately; deterministic, no injected noise, no entropy claim

Most first-pass requests were refused at launch by the shared fleet's BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_INSTANCES cap; every 8-unit request that did run hit the fleet's 3600 s job poweroff and returned all units as batch_job_timeout with no measurements; several clients were stopped by outer wall-clock limits while their jobs kept running (klt sim batch has no re-attach, so those results were never collected). Three first-pass requests returned and are reused verbatim because their request and netlist bytes are identical to the 3-unit packaging (marked 'reused'). The record's rows come only from the 3-unit request set; no other attempt below contributed a unit.
